decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts build directly on the firm's polishing, drilling and wafer-bonding know-how, and its in-house R&D lets it learn from early results and refine the product.
Carrier wafers fit squarely within the firm's established carrier and thin-wafer handling business, so it can interpret customer feedback and improve the product at low cost.
The copper interposer glass wafer is a flagship that extends the firm's packaging-wafer expertise, and its own R&D and EU research projects give it the related knowledge to develop it further.
The off-the-shelf brand for glass and quartz wafers is a flagship line very close to the core offer, which makes it easy to absorb market signals and keep it running.

Glass-based circuit boards lie far from the firm's wafer-substrate knowledge, which limits its ability to interpret results and learn from them, so resources are better redirected to core packaging wafers.
